instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

hint.text: The light brown areas on the map show deciduous woodland, and the dark brown areas show coniferous woodland.

atoms.text: There are two types of woodland biome: coniferous and deciduous.
atoms.sound: There are two types of woodland bye-ohm: coniferous and deciduous.

atoms.text: Deciduous woodlands have a temperate climate, which means they have four seasons, like in the UK. They consist of broad-leaved trees that shed their leaves in winter. These woodlands are home to animals such as deer, mice and foxes.
Coniferous woodlands can have both polar and temperate climates. They have evergreen trees with needles instead of leaves, as well as animals like brown bears, owls and squirrels.

atoms.a: What are the two types of woodland called?
What type of climate do deciduous woodlands have?
Which type of trees can be found in coniferous woodlands?

feedback.end: There is a large area of deciduous woodland in Japan — around 70% of the entire country!

instruction.text: The climate of the woodland in Japan is temperate. What does this mean?

feedback.end: As the trees here are deciduous, their leaves change colour and start to fall from the trees in autumn.

instruction.text: The Japanese woodlands are home to many different species of animal. Select the image that matches the description.

atoms.a: This unique type of goat-antelope is found in dense woodland. It is a national symbol of Japan.
This species of monkey is native to the north of Japan. They have thick fur to help with the cold temperatures there.
This bear spends most of its time in regions with higher altitudes, where it is cooler.
